Product browse11759%https://champssports.com/category/back-to-school.html
Champs Back to School Essentials is a 998-result merchandised grid with strong tile-level ratings and price signals but no hero offer or creative continuity from the ad.
Landing-page analysis
Page intent: Absorb back-to-school ad traffic into a very large merchandised grid of sneakers, backpacks and apparel and let the shopper self-select a product, with FLX Rewards sign-up as a secondary conversion.
Primary CTA: Add to bag / product tile click
Offer: $10 OFF SELECT BACKPACKS inline promo tile; scattered SALE price strikethroughs; site-wide 'Back to School Styles - Shop the Essentials' banner
Message match: Strong thematic match for a back-to-school sneaker ad - the H1 literally says Back to School Essentials and the assortment spans shoes, backpacks and apparel. Match weakens for any ad featuring a specific model or offer, since the shopper lands on a 998-result grid with no reinforcement of the ad's hero product.
Trust: Star ratings and review counts on nearly every tile, FLX Rewards program with free shipping messaging, Find a Store / store pickup availability, Klarna installment payments referenced site-wide
Friction: 998 results with no curated hero or editorial guidance at the top, Filters are collapsed behind a 'Show Filters' control rather than a persistent left rail, Sorting defaults to 'Featured' with no back-to-school-specific sort, Promotional interstitial tile ($10 off backpacks) interrupts the grid mid-scroll
What works
  • Category chip row (Men's, Women's, Kids', Clothing, Black & White Shoes, Backpacks) gives fast audience-based narrowing
  • Price, color-count swatches and ratings visible on every tile for quick scanning
  • Deal badges and strikethrough pricing create visible value without a hard discount claim
What it misses
  • No single dominant offer or urgency device at the top of the page
  • No back-to-school hero banner tying the page back to the ad creative
  • Kids' sizing - the core back-to-school need - is not surfaced above the fold
Product detail126%https://champssports.com/product/~/014ALBST.html
Champs HOKA Bondi 9 Wide PDP is well-built - strong gallery, ratings, wide-width callout, Klarna - but opens with a 'no longer available' banner, a half-struck-through size run and an explicit discount exclusion.
Landing-page analysis
Page intent: Sell a single women's HOKA Bondi 9 Wide running shoe, with size selection, ship-to-me or ship-to-store fulfillment, and Add to bag as the sole conversion action.
Primary CTA: Add to bag
Offer: None - 'Excluded from discount' is stated explicitly; Klarna and PayPal 4-interest-free-payments available on $30-$1500
Message match: Product-level match would be precise, but the page is topped by 'The product you are trying to view is no longer available.' - so the ad's specific colorway or SKU no longer resolves and the shopper sees a substitute PDP. Message match is therefore broken at the SKU level even though the model and category are right.
Trust: 4.4 star rating from 16 reviews, 45-day returns and exchanges, Free standard delivery, Klarna and PayPal installment options
Friction: 'The product you are trying to view is no longer available' banner at the very top undermines confidence before the shopper sees anything else, Roughly half the size run is struck through as unavailable (5.0, 6.0, 6.5, 8.5, 10.5, 11.0, 12.0), 'Excluded from discount' kills any promo-code expectation set by the ad, $175 full price with no financing emphasis above the fold
What works
  • Strong five-image product gallery including outsole and top-down detail
  • Wide-width fit is called out explicitly in the title and under Select a size
  • Dual fulfillment choice (ship to me vs ship to store) presented as a clear toggle
What it misses
  • No inventory or urgency signal on the sizes that are still available
  • No 'notify me' capture on the struck-through sizes - lost demand
  • No cross-sell or 'similar HOKA styles' module to rescue the unavailable-product visit

Product browse11426%https://footlocker.com/category/sport/running.html
Foot Locker's running page is a 1157-result catalog dump with heavy discounting and two in-grid HOKA ad units, but no fit guidance or performance/lifestyle separation.
Landing-page analysis
Page intent: Convert running-intent traffic into footwear and apparel sales across a very large assortment, while monetizing brand partnerships through in-grid HOKA banner placements.
Primary CTA: Add to bag / product tile click
Offer: Up to 30% off Nike & Jordan (site-wide top banner); dense SALE badging with strikethrough pricing across the grid; HOKA co-branded 'Look What Smooth Can Do - Shop Clifton 11' placements
Message match: Reasonable for a general running ad - the H1 and assortment are on-topic. But at 1157 results the page is effectively a catalog dump, and the assortment blends performance running (Vomero, Pegasus, Clifton) with lifestyle runners (Air Max 95, Samba, 9060), so a shopper from a performance-specific ad wades through lifestyle product.
Trust: Ratings and review counts on tiles, Ready, Set, Go running editorial banner at the top, HOKA brand-partner placements lending category credibility, FLX Rewards free shipping and rewards messaging
Friction: 1157 results - the largest and least curated page in the set, Two separate HOKA ad units interrupt the product grid, Filters collapsed behind 'Show Filters', Performance and lifestyle running are not separated
What works
  • Ready, Set, Go banner gives an editorial entry point tied to back-to-school running
  • Deep discount density creates an immediate value impression
  • Ratings on nearly every tile support confident self-selection
What it misses
  • No shoe finder, gait guide or filter-by-cushioning - the key running conversion tools
  • In-grid HOKA ad units push a competing product against the shopper's original intent
  • No consolidated running-specific offer despite heavy tile-level discounting
Product detail143%https://footlocker.com/product/~/00151181.html
Foot Locker's Birkenstock Arizona PDP has the set's best social proof at 4.9 stars but is undercut by an unavailable-product banner, a discount exclusion beneath a 30%-off banner, and a sandal miscategorized under Outdoor Shoes.
Landing-page analysis
Page intent: Sell a single men's Birkenstock Arizona colorway with size selection, dual fulfillment options and Add to bag as the sole conversion action.
Primary CTA: Add to bag
Offer: None - 'Excluded from discount'; free standard delivery; Klarna and PayPal 4-interest-free-payments on $30-$1500
Message match: Poor at the SKU level and questionable at the category level. The page opens with 'The product you are trying to view is no longer available', and a Birkenstock sandal is a weak destination for sneaker or back-to-school creative. The breadcrumb also miscategorizes the sandal under Outdoor Shoes.
Trust: 4.9 star rating from 52 reviews - the highest rating in the set, 45-day returns and exchanges, Free standard delivery, Klarna and PayPal installment options
Friction: 'The product you are trying to view is no longer available' banner at the top of the page, Sizes 7.0 and 13.0 struck through as unavailable, 'Excluded from discount' contradicts the 30%-off banner running directly above it, Only three product images - the thinnest gallery of the PDPs reviewed
What works
  • 4.9 stars from 52 reviews is exceptionally strong social proof placed right above the price
  • Most of the size run (8.0 through 12.0) is in stock and selectable
  • Free standard delivery is unconditional rather than gated behind rewards membership
What it misses
  • No cross-sell or similar-styles module to recover the unavailable-product visit
  • No 'notify me' capture on the struck-through sizes
  • The 4.9 rating is not amplified - no review quote is surfaced near the buy box
